q1_issues.issue: The trigger clause sits in the rule PREMISE as a Skolem-function term `(sk_tend $x)`, which no asserted tending event can ever match, so the rule can never fire on an actual occurrence — the whenever pattern puts an ordinary event variable in the premise and uses a Skolem function only in the consequent.

The drawn "stored mire-essence" is a single top-level constant witness asserted outside the conditional, so the parse asserts as a standing fact that a specific quantity of stored mire-essence exists, and shares one portion across every Keeper and every occasion where the dependent-existential (Skolem-function) form is called for.

q2_gaps: habitual "when <clause>" whose main clause has a definite-plural (group) subject: the whenever construction ranges over occurrences while the group-distribution rule ranges over members, and the instruction set never says how to combine the two ranges in one Implication (or that a bare "when", as opposed to "every time / whenever", triggers the rule form at all — "when" is otherwise listed as a temporal connective keeping the canonical Time-section forms)
a capitalized definite plural naming an in-world order ("the Keepers"): proper noun (name-derived constant + Name atom) versus ordinary definite-plural group witness is not adjudicated
notes: No Name atom is emitted for the capitalized "Keepers". The mire_essence genus, the participle-as-adjective `stored`, and the Patient/Theme role choices all follow the instruction set.
